title: Early Life Exposure to Manure-Fertilized Soil Shapes the Gut Antibiotic Resistome.
ehr_evidence: The study used metagenomic sequencing of soil and mouse gut fecal samples (raw data publicly available under accession number PRJNA1206751); no electronic or computerized health records were analyzed.
summary: A controlled experimental mouse study raising pregnant BALB/c mice from birth in pig manure-fertilized red (Ultisols) or black (Mollisols) soils versus unfertilized controls and sampling gut microbiomes at 8 weeks, showing that early-life manure-fertilized soil exposure enriches gut antibiotic resistance genes, particularly tet(Q).
key_findings: Manure application increased soil ARG abundance: Manured RS 0.63 ± 0.03 copies/cell (10.5% increase over RS 0.57 ± 0.005, P < 0.05) and Manured BS 0.45 ± 0.02 copies/cell (12.5% increase over BS 0.40 ± 0.02, P < 0.05).

Gut ARG abundance was markedly higher in manured-exposed mice: Manured RS 3.34 ± 0.34 copies/cell (48.4% increase over RS 2.25 ± 0.37) and Manured BS 3.89 ± 0.62 copies/cell (109% increase over BS 1.86 ± 0.54).
Tetracycline resistance genes dominated the gut resistome (84.9% of gut-resident ARGs), with tet(Q) the most dominant subtype, constituting 90% of tetracycline ARGs.
Manure-amended soils increased gut MGE abundance: Manured RS 34.21 ± 2.47 copies/cell (12.5% higher than RS 30.51 ± 3.29) and Manured BS 36.07 ± 4.43 copies/cell (19.8% higher than BS 30.1 ± 6.91).
Procrustes analysis revealed a significant correlation between ARGs and gut microbiome composition (M2 = 0.39, P = 0.001); Muribaculaceae and Bacteroidaceae were identified as key hosts of tet(Q).
Relative abundance of ARGs in the gut microbiota of mice living in fertilized soils was 4.6–8.7 times greater than in the soils.
captured_features: tet(Q), tet(33), tet(37) tetracycline subtype abundances
gut microbiome composition (phylum and family level)
study_design: controlled experimental animal study (early-life exposure cohort in mice)
population: BALB/c mice exposed from birth (pregnant dams at 18 days gestation) to 8 weeks of age
limitations: Very small sample size (n = 3 mice per group)
Mouse model not directly translatable to humans
Described as a pilot study with limited human generalizability
data_availability_statement: The raw metagenomic sequence data are publicly available under the accession number PRJNA1206751.
